column3: NASB follows the critical text, without “for us”; “mind” is rendered “purpose,” and “has done with” “has ceased from.”
NASB follows the critical text (no “us,” “the desire,” “to have carried out”); NASB supplies “already” and renders “orgies” as “carousals.”
“Think it strange” is rendered “are surprised,” and “overflow of debauchery” “excess of dissipation.”
NASB supplies “the gospel” and “the will of.”
“Has drawn near” is rendered “is at hand”; “be clear-minded … sober” is rendered “be of sound judgment and sober spirit.”
NASB follows the critical text; it restructures “having fervent love among yourselves” as “keep fervent in your love for one another.”
“A gift” is rendered “a special gift”; NASB supplies “employ it.”
“Oracles” is rendered “utterances”; NASB supplies “let him speak” and “let him do so,” and renders “power” as “dominion.”
NASB follows the critical text, without the Textus Receptus ending (“on their part He is blasphemed, but on your part He is glorified”).
NASB follows the critical text (“in that name”); it supplies “suffers.”
“The house” is rendered “the household”; NASB supplies “it begins.”
The quotation is in capitals; “where will appear” is rendered “what will become of.”
NASB follows the critical text; “commit” is rendered “entrust.”
